newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cemig Q1 net slips to 26.7 mln reais.
newsitem.headline: Cemig Q1 net slips to 26.7 mln reais.

text.p: Brazilian power firm Cemig, owned by the state of Minas Gerais, released the following financial results for 1997's first quarter.
NOTE: Figures in Brazilian reais, not adjusted for inflation.
In a statement, the company said its first quarter net profit adjusted for inflation was 68.2 million reais compared to 79.9 million reais in the same period last year.

Cemig's Finance and Market Relations Director Francisco Luiz Moreira Penna was quoted as saying the decline in profits was due to growth in operating expenses relative to sales, given the lack of a rate adjustment between November 1995 and March 1997.
He said electricity sales grew 6.7 percent and receipts rose seven percent, but average inflation in the period was 15 percent as measured by the Getulio Vargas Foundation's IGP-M index.

The cost of buying power from Itaipu dam, which rose 14.7 percent, was one of the main factors contributing to the rise in operating expenses, as the purchases are in dollars and subject to exchange rate variations, the statement said.
Despite the increase, however, Cemig's operating cost of 45 reais per megawatt remains low compared to other large Brazilian utilities.

Costs also were driven higher by a 5.97 percent wage hike for workers. However, Cemig's payroll has dropped 7.2 percent to 14,739 employees at the end of the quarter from 15,878 workers on March 31, 1996.
"The number of customers per employee has risen 13 percent to 292 compared with the same period last year," Penna said.
Cemig's total debt at the end of the first quarter was 1.036 billion reais, of which 59 percent was in foreign currency, and equalled 11.7 percent of net worth, the statement said.
The company's net worth totalled 9.996 billion reais in 1997's first three months compared with 9.893 billion reais in the period last year.
